Why did `DAYOFWEEK(starts_at)` say 340 out of 340 `daily`, 4139 out of 4169 `weekly`, 4465 out of 4547 `every_other_week` are drifted?!
Let's check what `DAYOFWEEK(starts_at)` returns in this SQL engine! In DuckDB/Postgres/ISO, what does `DAYOFWEEK` return vs `EXTRACT(DOW FROM starts_at)`?
Look at the sample rows from earlier:
- Row id 3564: `frequency='every_other_week'`, `day_one='4'`, `starts_at='2021-07-07T00:00:00'`.
What day of the week was `2021-07-07`?!
July 7, 2021 was a WEDNESDAY! With Sunday = 1, Monday = 2, Tuesday = 3, Wednesday = 4!
And `day_one` is `4`! So row 3564 is NOT drifted!
Why did `DAYOFWEEK('2021-07-07')` not equal 4? Because in DuckDB, `DAYOFWEEK` (or `ISODOW`) returns Sunday=0, Monday=1, Tuesday=2, Wednesday=3! So `DAYOFWEEK('2021-07-07') + 1` is 4 (Sunday=1..Saturday=7)!
